# Secrets

Real secret values are never written into documentation, logs, issues or chat. This page lists the
files, who consumes them, and how to rotate them.

## Files generated by `scripts/generate-secrets.mjs`

`npm run secrets:generate` (equivalent to `node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs`) writes into `./secrets`, or
into `ORC_SECRETS_DIR` or `--dir <dir>`. The directory is gitignored. Existing files are kept unless you
pass `--force`, which replaces everything, or `--only <names> --force`, which replaces only the named files.

| File | Kind | Consumers (compose secret → `/run/secrets/<name>`) |
|---|---|---|
| `mssql_sa_password.txt` | 32-character SQL password | `mssql` (entrypoint and healthcheck), `db-bootstrap`; restore runs as sa inside mssql. Used nowhere else. |
| `db_migrator_password.txt` | SQL password | db-bootstrap (sets it), migrator, db-cli |
| `db_api_password.txt` | SQL password | db-bootstrap, api |
| `db_worker_password.txt` | SQL password | db-bootstrap, worker |
| `db_backup_password.txt` | SQL password | db-bootstrap; read on the host by `scripts/backup.mjs` |
| `redis_password.txt` | 43-character base64url token | redis (`requirepass`, through a tmpfs config file), api, worker |
| `egress_proxy_token.txt` | 43-character base64url token | egress-proxy (`EGRESS_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE`), worker (`EGRESS_PROXY_TOKEN_FILE`). Given only to Claude processes, as proxy credentials. |
| `claude_oauth_token.txt` | supplied by the operator: `claude setup-token`, then `--only claude_oauth_token --claude-oauth-token-stdin` | worker only (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE`). Reaches Claude only through the runner socket and file descriptor 3. Empty (0 bytes) = not configured. |
| `anthropic_api_key.txt` | supplied by the operator for `CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE=api_key` only (`--anthropic-api-key-stdin`) | worker only. Passed only to Claude processes. Empty (0 bytes) = not configured. |
| `web_ca_cert.pem` / `web_ca_key.pem` | local web CA (10 years) | Not mounted. Import the certificate into browsers. The key signs the server certificate. |
| `web_tls_cert.pem` / `web_tls_key.pem` | EC P-256 server certificate (825 days), SAN `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `WEB_SERVER_NAME`, `--san` | web (nginx, TLS on 8443) |
| `db_ca_cert.pem` / `db_ca_key.pem` | private SQL Server CA | The certificate goes to api, worker, db-bootstrap, migrator and db-cli (`DB_CA_CERT_FILE`). The key is not mounted. |
| `mssql_tls_cert.pem` / `mssql_tls_key.pem` | RSA 3072 server certificate, SAN `mssql` | mssql (`docker/mssql/mssql.conf`) |

Passwords use the alphabet of `SQL_LOGIN_PASSWORD_REGEX` (contract §4.2): no quotes, brackets, backslash,
`$` or whitespace. `scripts/compose-check.mjs` (run by `compose:config` and `compose:up`) checks that every
referenced file exists and matches the rule enforced by its service. It also checks that the PEM files
parse and that each server certificate chains to its CA.

The **runner receives no secret at all**. The sandboxed processes (Claude children, tests, MCP) never see
the DB or Redis credentials. `npm run test:compose` proves this.

## Permissions

- POSIX hosts: the directory is `0700`, owned by the operator. Secret files are `0644`, so that the
  container users (node 1000, mssql 10001, nginx 101, redis 999) can read their bind-mounted copies. The
  CA keys are `0600`, because no container needs them.
- Windows / Docker Desktop: the files inherit the ACLs of the user profile. Keep the directory inside your
  profile, or protect `ORC_SECRETS_DIR` with ACLs that allow only the operator account.
- Back up the directory to an encrypted offline location. It cannot be regenerated with the same values.
- Never mount the directory anywhere else, and never copy it into an image or the build context. It is
  excluded by `.dockerignore`.

## Rotation

Before you rotate, generate the new value in a scratch directory or with `--only ... --force`. Commands
that recreate containers interrupt running attempts, which are then recovered automatically.

### DB login passwords (`db_migrator`, `db_api`, `db_worker`, `db_backup`)

```bash
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only db_api_password --force      # or several, comma-separated
npm run compose:up                                                     # db-bootstrap applies the new login passwords
docker compose restart api                                             # consumers re-read the file (worker for db_worker_password)
```

`db_backup_password` needs no restart; `backup.mjs` reads the file on each run.

### SQL Server `sa` password

The `mssql-data` volume keeps the old password, so change the login first, and replace the file second:

```bash
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --dir ./secrets-new --only mssql_sa_password --skip-certs
docker compose exec -T mssql /bin/bash -ec 'IFS= read -r NEWPW; export SQLCMDPASSWORD="$(cat /run/secrets/mssql_sa_password)"; printf "ALTER LOGIN sa WITH PASSWORD = N'"'"'%s'"'"';\nGO\n" "$NEWPW" | /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -C -b' < ./secrets-new/mssql_sa_password.txt
cp ./secrets-new/mssql_sa_password.txt ./secrets/mssql_sa_password.txt && rm -rf ./secrets-new
npm run compose:up
```

The new password travels over stdin. `printf` is a shell builtin, so the value never appears in a
process argument list.

### Redis password

```bash
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only redis_password --force
docker compose up -d --force-recreate redis api worker
```

AOF data survives the restart.

### Egress proxy token

```bash
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only egress_proxy_token --force
docker compose up -d --force-recreate egress-proxy worker
```

### Claude OAuth token

Renew (before expiry, or after a 401 / "Not logged in" failure) or rotate:

```bash
claude setup-token                                   # prints the new sk-ant-oat01-... token
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only claude_oauth_token --force --claude-oauth-token-stdin < /path/to/new-token
docker compose up -d --force-recreate worker         # the worker reads the file only at startup
```

Delete the temporary token file. Revoke the old token in your Claude account settings; `setup-token` tokens
stay valid until revoked or expired. An auth failure ends the attempt once; nothing retries it. Renew,
restart the worker, then submit the task again. The command refuses a malformed token and never prints it.

### Switching the auth mode

Exactly one credential file is non-empty and it must match `CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` (`oauth`, the default, or
`api_key`, not recommended: the key can reach the Bash children of agents that have Bash rules enabled).
`generate-secrets` refuses to write one credential while the other file is non-empty, and `compose-check`
refuses to start the stack otherwise.

```bash
# oauth -> api_key: empty both files, install the key, select the mode
: > secrets/anthropic_api_key.txt && : > secrets/claude_oauth_token.txt
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only anthropic_api_key --anthropic-api-key-stdin < /path/to/key-file
CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE=api_key npm run compose:up
```

For the reverse direction, empty both files, install the token and start with the default mode. Set
`CLAUDE_AUTH_MODE` in the shell or in `.env` for every `docker compose` call. Never set both credentials;
the worker and the runner reject that combination.

### Web TLS certificate

- For local use, regenerate: `node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only web --force [--web-server-name <host>] [--san <name>]`.
  Then run `docker compose restart web`. A new CA is created as well, so browsers must import the new
  `web_ca_cert.pem`.
- For an operator certificate, replace `web_tls_cert.pem` (full chain, PEM) and `web_tls_key.pem`
  (unencrypted PEM key), then run `docker compose restart web`. Set `PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://<host>:8443`
  and `WEB_BIND_ADDRESS` for remote access.

### SQL Server TLS (private CA)

```bash
node scripts/generate-secrets.mjs --only db --force
npm run compose:down && npm run compose:up
```

All DB clients verify the new CA after the restart.

### Users and tokens

User passwords are changed in the UI (**Account**). That revokes the user's other sessions. Personal
access tokens are revoked in **Account → Tokens**. Disabling a user revokes all of the user's sessions
and tokens.
